paper.title: An optimal algorithm for the Thresholding Bandit Problem

unmapped: Goal: after a fixed budget T, output the set of arms with mean above a known threshold tau, up to precision epsilon (arms within the 2*epsilon band carry no cost)
Loss is the probability of misclassifying any arm outside the band
settings.definition_quote: We define the $(\tau, \epsilon)$ thresholding problem as such : after $T$ rounds of the game described above, the goal of the learner is to correctly identify the \textit{arms whose means are over or under the threshold $\tau$ up to a certain precision $\epsilon$}, i.e.~to correctly discriminate arms that belong to $S_{\tau + \epsilon}$ from those in $S_{\tau-\epsilon}^C$.

settings.name_in_paper: Thresholding Bandit Problem, Gaussian instances (lower bound)
unmapped: Thresholding objective with threshold tau and precision epsilon
Learner may even know the gaps of all arms to the threshold
settings.definition_quote: For $0\leq i\leq K$, we write $\mathcal B^i$ for the problem where the distribution of arm $j\in \{1, \ldots, K\}$ is $\mathcal N(\tau+d_i+\epsilon,1)$ if $i \neq j$ and $\mathcal N(\tau-d_i-\epsilon,1)$ otherwise.

settings.name_in_paper: Thresholding Bandit Problem, R-sub-Gaussian class with complexity at most H-bar (lower bound)
unmapped: Thresholding objective with threshold tau and precision epsilon
Class of problems with complexity at most H_bar
settings.definition_quote: Consider $\mathbb B_{\bar H,R}$ the set of $K$-armed bandit problems where the distributions of the arms are $R$-sub-Gaussian and which have all a complexity smaller than $\bar H$.

settings.name_in_paper: Best arm identification (fixed budget) with known highest mean
settings.definition_quote: In the best arm identification problem, the game setting is the same as the one we considered but the goal of the learner is different: it aims at returning an arm $J_T$ that with the highest possible mean.

settings.name_in_paper: Cumulative reward maximization with known highest mean
settings.definition_quote: In the cumulative reward maximization problem, the game setting is the same as the the one we considered but the aim of the learner is different : if we write $X_t$ for the sample collected at time $t$ by the algorithm, it aims at maximizing $\sum_{t \leq T} X_t$.

symbols.H_tbp: complexity sum_i (|mu_i - tau| + epsilon)^{-2} (here sum_i (d_i + 2 epsilon)^{-2})

conditions: max over the K+1 Gaussian unit-variance problems B^0..B^K sharing the same gaps

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: It holds that for any bandit algorithm \max_{i \in \{0,\ldots,K\}} \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{B}^i}(\mathcal L(T)) \geq \exp\big(-3T/H-4\log(12(\log(T)+1)K)\big)

results.notes: Local minimax lower bound over a finite family with fixed gaps; expected loss equals probability of error.

symbols.H_bar: upper bound on the complexity H of problems in the class

conditions: sup over R-sub-Gaussian K-armed problems with complexity at most H_bar

source.label: cor:LB
source.quote: Assume that $T \geq 4\bar HR^2\log(12(\log(T)+1)K)$. It holds that for any bandit algorithm \sup_{\mathcal B \in \mathbb B_{\bar H, R}} \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{B}}(\mathcal L(T)) \geq \exp\big(-4T/(R^2\bar H)\big)

results.notes: R (sub-Gaussian constant) mapped to sigma. R^2 appears in the denominator as printed.

source.label: thm:UB
source.quote: Let $K \geq 0, T \geq 2K$, and consider a problem $\mathcal B$. Assume that all arms $\nu_k$ of the problem are $R$-sub-Gaussian with means $\mu_k$. Let $\tau \in \mathbb R, \epsilon \geq 0$ Algorithm APT's expected loss is upper bounded on this problem as $\mathbb E(\mathcal L(T)) \leq \exp\left(-\frac{1}{64R^2}\frac{T}{ H} + 2\log((\log(T)+1)K)\right)$

results.notes: APT needs neither T, R nor H; anytime.

symbols.H_bar: upper bound on the complexity H of problems in the class

conditions: sup over R-sub-Gaussian K-armed problems with complexity at most H_bar

source.label: cor:UB
source.quote: Assume that $T \geq 256 \bar HR^2\log((\log(T)+1)K)$. For Algorithm APT it holds that \sup_{\mathcal B \in \mathbb B_{\bar H, R}} \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{B}}(\mathcal L(T)) \leq \exp\big(-T/(128R^2H)\big)

results.notes: Paper prints H in the exponent; interpreted as H_bar since it is a sup over the class.

source.label: thm:Simple
source.quote: Then APT run with parameters $\tau = \mu^*$ and $\epsilon = 0$, recommending the arm $J_T = \arg\max_{k} T_k(T)$, is such that $\mathbb{P}(\mu_{J_T} \neq \mu^*) \leq \exp\big(-\frac{T}{36R^2H_{\mu^*}} + 2\log(\log(T)+1)K\big)$.

results.notes: H_{mu*} = sum over suboptimal arms of (mu*-mu_i)^{-2} = H_1. The log term is printed ambiguously as 2log(log(T)+1)K; recorded literally (proof suggests 2log((log T+1)K)).

source.label: thm:CR
source.quote: Then APT run with parameters $\tau = \mu^*$ and $\epsilon = 0$ is such that $T\mu^* - \mathbb E \sum_{t \leq T} X_t \leq \inf_{\delta \geq 1} \Big[\sum_{k \not = k^*} \frac{4R^2\log(T)\delta}{\mu^* - \mu_i} + (\mu^*- \mu_i)(1 + \frac{K}{T^{2\delta - 2}})\Big]$.

results.notes: Recorded the delta=1 instance of the infimum (a valid, possibly weaker, upper bound), as derived at the end of the proof. Regret T mu* - E sum X_t is pseudo-regret.
